- Stack entry `L4407508c.BRF120_60`, session NY AM (code 3, 09:30-12:00 ET), engine base set `TL3_ALN_NY_L4407508c_R0BRF120_60` (bare R0, 1 lot), events file `/mnt/l2/l2vast/_brkt/ev/L4407508c_R0_F120_60.parquet` (1,362 events, all side +1, stop 120.0, target 60.0, lots 1).
- Cell (engine ladder cell, found with brkt_build.find_cell): row `time_m_3`, module `trig_bands_bollinger`, variant `walk`, params {"n": 30, "k": 1.5, "N": 2}, own ladder bracket `asym10u/20u`, cell mode `long`. The stack uses the fixed bracket shape F120_60 (not the cell's own asym10u/20u) on the same trigger events.
- Weighted-stack weight 0.25 = 1 whole base lot (the table in D8_BUILD_SPEC.md says lots (base) 1). Lot sizing at the live file's 6 lots/book is a stack decision, open (section 9).

## 1. BAR rule (time_m_3): what the code does
Code: `outputs/code/th_bars/build_month.py` function `time_bars` lines 52-66, called at line 88 as `time_bars(ts,px,sz,side,iid,key,P*60)` with P = 3 (GRID['time_m'] line 9), so bucket length 180 s. Session split `sessionize()` in `outputs/code/th_bars/common.py` lines 10-17 (ET clock: code 0 Asia 18:00-02:00, 1 London 02:00-08:30, 2 pre 08:30-09:30, 3 NY AM 09:30-12:00, 4 NY PM 12:00-16:00, 5 close 16:00-18:00; trading date = ET + 6 h; session id = td x 10 + code). Rules:
1. Input = every trade record of the tape (one row per exchange trade record, no merge, no filter). Time bars are unaffected by the run-merge/print rule (D8_PRINT_RULE.md section 5 table, row time_m: UNAFFECTED).
2. A SEGMENT = a run of prints with the same session key (td x 10 + code) and the same instrument id (line 53 `newseg`). A new segment starts at every session boundary and at a contract roll. t_start = the timestamp of the FIRST print of the segment (line 54), NOT the clock boundary. For NY AM on both parity days the first print is at 09:30:00 ET to within a few microseconds (20261110: 14:30:00.000021317Z in the engine tape, so the grid edges are that instant + n x 180 s, not the exact clock minute); on a day whose first print is later, the whole 3-minute grid is shifted by that offset (not seen on the two days).
3. bucket k = floor((ts - t_start) / 180 s) (line 55). A bar exists only for buckets with at least one print (line 56 groups consecutive prints of the same segment and bucket).
4. Bar fields (lines 57-58): open = first print price, close = last print price, high/low = max/min print price in the bucket, volume = sum of `sz` (contracts), prices in ticks of 0.25 point in the store (the CSVs below are in points).
5. Known time (line 61-63): known = t_start + (k+1) x 180 s exactly (the bucket end), with no wait for the next print. The LAST bucket of a segment is truncated: if its last print is before the bucket end (always true at the NY AM end because there are no NY AM prints after 12:00), part = 1 and known = the last print's timestamp (e.g. 16:59:59.904Z on 20261110). A part = 1 bar stays in the series, but a signal on it is never traded (section 3, step 6): the book cannot fire on the final 3-minute bar 11:57-12:00 ET.
6. Result: 50 bars per NY AM session (49 full bars known at 09:33:00, 09:36:00, ... 11:57:00 ET, and the truncated bar 11:57-12:00 ET as bar 50 with part = 1). Verified on both parity days (50 rows each, below).
7. Series seen by the trigger: ALL sessions of all history concatenated in known-time order as one continuous series (D8_BAR_DEFS.md section 2, "Series seen by the signal code"; engine loader `outputs/code/th_grid/gjob.py` load_bars lines 33-49: sorted by t_close, part = 1 bars kept). So the indicator window of the first NY AM bars reaches back into the pre-market (session code 2, 20 bars of 08:30-09:30 ET) and London (code 1) bars. Checked: on both days the 29 bars before the first NY AM bar are 20 code-2 bars and 9 code-1 bars (all with 3-min grids anchored at their own session's first print).

## 2. TRIGGER rule (every constant)
Code: `outputs/code/th_grid/trig_bands_bollinger.py` lines 13-20 (`_bands`, plain branch lines 17-18) and `outputs/code/th_grid/bandlib_wgrida.py` lines 9-12 (variant parse), 49-51 (run_len), 53-68 (events), 75-87 (make), `outputs/code/th_grid/ind.py` lines 29-33 (sma), 35-47 (rolling_std, ddof 0). Parameters of this book: variant `walk` (not native, so plain bar-count lookback, no clock conversion), n = 30 bars, k = 1.5, N = 2. Input line: the bar CLOSE only (units: points).
For each bar j of the continuous series (all sessions):
- mid_j = simple mean of the 30 closes c[j-29..j] (the window INCLUDES the current bar j).
- s_j = POPULATION standard deviation (divide by 30, ddof = 0) of the same 30 closes.
- upper_j = mid_j + 1.5 x s_j; lower_j = mid_j - 1.5 x s_j. Both are undefined (NaN) until 30 bars exist in the series (irrelevant for live: the series starts 2023-04-02).
- outside-up_j = (close_j > upper_j), strict greater; outside-down_j = (close_j < lower_j), strict less; NaN bands count as not outside.
- run_up_j = number of consecutive bars ending at j that were outside-up (0 if bar j is not outside-up). LONG event at bar j when run_up_j == 2 exactly: the 2nd consecutive close above the upper band. A 3rd, 4th ... consecutive close does NOT fire again; a new run (after a close that is not above the band) can fire again at its 2nd bar. The test for each bar compares the close with that bar's OWN band (the band moves with the window, it is not frozen at the first outside bar).
- SHORT event mirrored (run_down_j == 2). A bar that is both long and short is dropped (cannot occur with k > 0). THE BOOK TRADES LONG ONLY: short events exist in the engine's raw signal list (10,934 of them) and are discarded by the stack entry (cell mode `long`, brkt_build.py line 47 `if mode in ('long','short')`). Do not code the short side.
- Computed at bar close (bar known time); no look-ahead.
- Window state needed by a coder: 31 prior closes (30 for the band at bar j, one more for the previous bar's outside flag); the run counter needs the previous bar's outside flag, which is computed with that bar's own window. The window runs across session and weekend breaks (continuous series).

## 3. From signal to order (events pipeline, engine code)
`outputs/code/th_brkt/brkt_build.py` raw_events lines 34-42 and make lines 43-48:
1. signals = the module's long and short flips on the full series; 2. keep a signal only if the signal bar has part == 0 AND its session code == 3 (NY AM) (line 38-39); 3. order time `ts` = floor(bar known time to whole seconds) + 2 s (line 42, `t // 10**9 + 2`); 4. `exit_ts` = the end of the signal bar's ET session = 12:00 ET (16:00/17:00 UTC) (line 42 `TC.sess_end_ns`; th_swap/common.py lines 32-40); 5. drop events with ts >= exit_ts (line 46); 6. keep side +1 only (cell mode long, line 47); 7. stop 120.0 and target 60.0 points on every event (SHAPES['F120_60'] line 19, applied at line 44: `(120.0, 60.0)` = (stop, target)); lots 1; 8. `cap_exit.cap_events`: if no print follows the scheduled exit within 120 s, the exit is the last print before it (th_fakefill/cap_exit.py lines 20-39).
Verified: my independent re-implementation of steps 1-6 from the stored bars gives 1,362 events whose times equal the stored events file (all 1,362, side +1).

## 4. SIDES, BRACKET, UNITS
- Side: LONG only (buy). Short events are discarded.
- Bracket: STOP 120 points and TARGET 60 points, measured from the FILL price, in NQ POINTS (1 point = 4 ticks of 0.25 = $20 per contract; stop = 480 ticks = $2,400, target = 240 ticks = $1,200 per contract). Fixed, no per-bar unit (no "u" rule, nothing scaled by range) for this entry, even though the cell's own bracket label is asym10u/20u. Verified in the events file (every one of 1,362 events 120.0 / 60.0) and in TRADES of 20261027 (target exits +60.0 exactly; the one stop exit realised -119.0 points; the 1-point difference to 120 is engine fill mechanics and is not explained here).
- Session-end exit: scheduled flat at 12:00 ET (17:00 UTC in EST, 16:00 UTC in EDT) = `exit_ts`.

## 5. OTHER-MARKET OR LEVEL INPUTS
None. The trigger uses only the book's own 3-minute closes (DATA_NEED 'none' in the module). No other market, no price level, no VWAP line, no scale table (time bars have no scale factor).

## 6. ONE-POSITION RULE, SESSION WINDOW
- One position per book: an event whose order time falls while the book is in a trade, an exit is pending or an entry is in flight is dropped; no other re-entry rule (D8_BUILD_SPEC.md (b2), engine sim). The events file is NOT a trade list. Seen in the data below: 20261027 has 5 events but 4 trades; the 14:51:02Z event is skipped because the trade entered at 14:36:03Z is still open (it exits at 15:00:53Z at the target).
- Session window: signals from NY AM bars only, i.e. bars known after 09:33:00 ET up to the last full bar (11:57:00 ET); the order of the last possible signal is 11:57:02 ET; everything open is flat at 12:00 ET.

## 7. Entry, fill and exit mechanics (quoted from the engine description, not re-derived)
From the hand-written blocks in D8_BUILD_SPEC.md (b2) (e.g. AUTO:BOOK:L7cc56d99) and the parity pages: MARKET order sent at `ts` (= known time floored to the second + 2 s), filled 1.0 s later (LAT_FILL) at the 10-level book state, buy at the ask side walking the levels; stop = stop order at fill - 120 pts triggered by a print at or through the level then a market order; target = resting limit at fill + 60 pts; scheduled session-end exit at 12:00 ET executed 1.0 s later (UWTime), last print before it if no print follows within 120 s. Consistency check on the four TRADES rows of 20261027 (this page, section 8): each entry time = order time + 1.000 s exactly; both targets filled at exactly entry + 60.00; the UWTime exit is at 16:00:01.000Z (12:00 ET + 1 s). The fill price walking the book is NOT reproducible from bars; it needs the book (10-level) data.

## 8. Parity data, td 20261027 (EDT, NY AM = 13:30-16:00 UTC) and td 20261110 (EST, NY AM = 14:30-17:00 UTC)
Times are UTC, millisecond resolution. Prices in points. BARS = the 50 NY AM time_m_3 bars of the engine store (`/mnt/l2/l2vast/_bars/time_m_3/202610.parquet`, `202611.parquet`); the last row of each has part = 1. SIGNALS = the stored events file rows for that td (order time = bar known time floored + 2 s). INPUTS = the 29 bars before the NY AM open (all sessions) plus the 50 NY AM bars (79 rows), with the indicator values my independent code computed (and which equal the engine module's values at the signal bars). TRADES = engine exact-set trades of the bare 1-lot book run (base set above).

2. Stack-level layers (locks, give-back, day halts, stack rules, weights as whole lots) are NOT part of this page: weighted-stack joint fit of STKd8cd0279ff not posted (NYAM_FINAL_STATUS.md section 4). The live file runs 6 lots/book; the stack weight 0.25 is 1 base lot of the x4 engine basis; the whole-lot size at the live file is open for LEAD.
3. Entry/fill walk of the book and the stop-slip are engine mechanics given as described, not re-derived here.
4. NT8: whether NT8's Bollinger indicator uses the population standard deviation (the engine does, ddof 0) was not checked; the rule above is the engine's and a coder should implement it literally (own SMA and population std on the 3-minute closes of the session-restarting grid) rather than rely on a built-in. The 3-minute grid restarts at each session's first print (not a fixed NT8 session template); equivalence to an NT8 session template was not tested here.
5. Roll days: a contract roll starts a new segment (grid restarts, session key + instrument id); engine skips entries from roll - 120 s to roll + 300 s and is flat 1 ns before the roll second (D8_BUILD_SPEC.md (b2)). No roll inside the two parity days.
6. Exit verdicts: NYAM_FINAL_STATUS.md section 3: one exit recipe (flow_v25) passes stage 1 for this book but loses money (L6M mean -$141 versus +$1,526 bare); no exit kept.

## Relay questions 2026-11-24 21:25Z (answers added by W-NYAMSPEC2; engine files untouched)
Q2a. Your reading (mid = SMA of the last 30 closes including the current bar; population sd, ddof 0; upper = mid + 1.5 sd; LONG on the bar whose run of consecutive closes above its own band equals exactly 2; continuous series across sessions including truncated part = 1 bars): CORRECT on every point. The truncated bar stays in the window and in the run count; only a SIGNAL on it is not traded. Short flips are discarded.
Q2b. Bar counts: the stored 20261110 NY AM series is 50 rows = 49 full 3-minute bars (known 09:33:00 ... 11:57:00 ET) + 1 truncated bar (part = 1); your 49 are the full bars.
Q2c. Bucket-edge rule (code th_bars/build_month.py time_bars lines 52-66; tape th_bars/extract_trades.py line 1): timestamp field = `ts_event` (exchange event time, integer ns UTC) of every MBO record with action T (trade). Grid anchor t_start = ts_event of the FIRST trade record of the session segment (20261110 NY AM: 14:30:00.000021317Z in the engine tape; hist_replica shows the same first trade at 14:30:00.002894864Z). bucket k = floor((ts_event - t_start) / 180e9 ns): a record exactly on an edge belongs to the NEW bucket (start INCLUSIVE, end EXCLUSIVE; 3 such records on 20261110 NY AM). Bar known time = t_start + (k+1) x 180 s. Sensitivity measured on 20261110 NY AM (234,912 records, same count in both files): 90 records fall within 15 ms after an edge and 12 within 15 ms before. Rebuilding with the same rule from the hist_replica timestamps (anchor = its first record) gives 6 bars different from the stored ones (bar numbers 10, 11, 30, 31, 43, 44, 1-based) and anchoring on the exact 14:30:00.000 clock gives 2 different bars (the first two). So bucket-edge differences of the size you see are expected whenever the timestamp field or the anchor differs; the engine numbers are the ones above. I do not have your 8 differing bars and did not check them (not verified).
